what_it_is.summary: This is a small GPT-2-style decoder, the classic layout behind the first widely known text generators: 3 layers stacked one on another, each word held as a list of 16 numbers, 2 attention heads looking at the text in parallel. It reads at most 12 words at a time; anything earlier is invisible to it. It departs from the standard GPT-2 layout in 1 place, explained below.

components.name: Family
components.label: gpt2
components.plain: a small GPT-2-style decoder, the classic layout behind the first widely known text generators

components.name: Attention
components.label: surprise-routed
components.plain: a small predictor guesses each word in advance; words it finds surprising get full attention and predictable ones take a cheaper summarising path
components.technical: the softmax-normalised query-key similarities that mix values

components.name: Word positions
components.label: learned
components.plain: the model learns one marker for each position in the text
components.technical: the function of index that tells attention where tokens are

components.name: Normalisation
components.label: LayerNorm
components.plain: each word's internal numbers are re-centred and rescaled to keep them in a stable range (layer normalisation)

components.name: Feed-forward switch
components.label: GELU
components.plain: the feed-forward layers use a smooth on/off switch (GELU) to decide which internal features fire
components.technical: the per-token feed-forward block, read as a key-value memory

components.name: Layer shortcuts
components.label: residual
components.plain: each layer adds its result on top of what came in, so information can pass straight through (a residual shortcut)
components.technical: the additive skip pathway every block writes into

components.name: Optimiser
components.label: AdamW
components.plain: trained with AdamW, the standard optimiser, which adjusts each weight with its own step size
components.technical: the per-parameter moment estimates kept during training

what_to_expect.summary: Text in the style of its training corpus; how coherent it is depends on the corpus, which this card could not identify. Its best validation loss of 1.89 suggests mostly grammatical short phrases within its domain (a rough guide only: loss is not comparable across corpora or vocabularies). With 11 thousand parameters it is tiny: the assistants people chat with every day are at least a thousand times larger.
can: continue text in the style of its training data
